test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 24 Dec, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Two trains, 125 m and 165 m in length, respectively, are running in opposite directions, one at the rate of 80 km/h and the other at the rate of 65 km/h. In how many seconds will they be completely clear of each other from the moment they meet?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__
**Relative Speed** in opposite direction = 80 + 65 = 145 km/h.

Convert km/h to m/s: 145 × (5/18) m/s.

**Total Distance** = 125 + 165 = 290 m.

Time = 290 ÷ [145 × (5/18)] = (290 × 18) ÷ (145 × 5) = 2 × 18 ÷ 5 = 36 ÷ 5 = 7.2 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is 7.2 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2878d5e6122b93726503819fc5cf911f8001377c24f720592ede54f27154f5b9.png] 
**Given:**

Length of **Train 1** (L₁) = 125 m

Length of **Train 2** (L₂) = 165 m

Speed of **Train 1** (S₁) = 80 km/h

Speed of **Train 2** (S₂) = 65 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (Opposite) = S₁ + S₂

Time = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = L₁ + L₂ = 125 + 165 = 290 m

⇒ Relative Speed = 80 + 65 = 145 km/h

⇒ Relative Speed in m/s = 145 × (5/18) = 725/18 m/s

⇒ Time = 290 ÷ (725/18)

⇒ Time = (290 × 18) ÷ 725

⇒ Time = 5220 ÷ 725 = 7.2 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 7.2 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Rules

When moving in **opposite directions**, speeds are added (S₁ + S₂). When moving in the **same direction**, speeds are subtracted (S₁ − S₂).

Unit Conversion

To convert **km/h to m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m/s to km/h**, multiply by 18/5.

Train Crossing Concepts

When a train crosses another train, the **total distance** traveled is the sum of the lengths of both trains.</p
